articles.title: Democratic Congress Puts AI Spending and Chip Export Controls Under New Scrutiny
articles.excerpt: With Democrats back in control of Congress, analysts expect tighter scrutiny of AI chip exports to China, new cost rules for large data centres, and investigations into the tariff and investment deals of the Trump administration.
articles.image_caption: A Samsung flag and the SK hynix logo at a company building. South Korea’s chipmakers face tighter scrutiny of AI chip exports and US investment pledges after the Democratic midterm victory.
articles.nri_angle: Indian investors holding US AI and chip stocks, and professionals in the Asian semiconductor supply chain, face a new oversight regime in Washington.

articles.title: Cabinet Clears Rs 14,500 Crore Storage Fund Backing 92 GWh of New Grid Capacity
articles.excerpt: The viability gap funding scheme covers 60 GWh of pumped hydro, 30 GWh of battery storage and 2 GWh of alternative technologies through 2030-31, against an estimated total investment of Rs 97,600 crore.
articles.image_caption: Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw speaks at a press briefing in New Delhi. The Cabinet approved Rs 14,500 crore in viability gap funding for 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage.
articles.nri_angle: The scheme is a direct read on where India grid-scale storage orders will flow over the next five years, relevant to diaspora investors in Indian power and battery supply chains.

articles.title: Pfizer Earnings Beat Estimates as Eliquis Growth Offsets COVID Decline, Guidance Raised
articles.excerpt: Third-quarter revenue of $16.58 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.87 topped consensus, and Pfizer lifted its full-year revenue outlook by $1.5 billion at the midpoint.
articles.image_caption: Pfizer's headquarters in New York. The drugmaker beat earnings estimates as Eliquis growth offset declining COVID product sales, and raised its guidance.
articles.nri_angle: Pfizer is a widely held U.S. large-cap stock, so its raised outlook and steady dividend are relevant to diaspora investors holding broad U.S. index and retirement portfolios.

articles.title: What the Midterms Could Mean for Markets, Debt and AI Stocks
articles.excerpt: Investors expect divided government, which history says stocks like — but a $40 trillion debt load and a 2027 debt-limit deadline make this cycle different.
articles.image_caption: The US Capitol in Washington. Voters decide control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections, with investors watching what divided or unified government means for federal debt and AI spending.
articles.nri_angle: Midterm control of Congress shapes US yields, the dollar and AI stocks that dominate many Indian American retirement portfolios.

articles.title: Royal Enfield Posts Record Festive Sales of 2.67 Lakh Motorcycles

articles.title: Binance Sets Aside $6.34 Billion After $6.3 Billion Hack, the Largest Crypto Theft Ever
articles.excerpt: Attackers drained about $6.3 billion from Binance's hot wallets in roughly 20 minutes on Thursday, in what the exchange traced to a compromised engineer's laptop. Binance says customer balances will be restored one-for-one, $3 billion of the stolen assets have been frozen, and withdrawals are expected to resume by Sunday.
articles.nri_angle: Indian crypto holders with Binance accounts are directly affected by the withdrawal pause; balances are promised one-for-one restoration, but withdrawals stay paused until security checks finish, expected by Sunday.

articles.title: India's Fiscal Deficit Hits Rs 7.14 Lakh Crore, 42.1% of Full-Year Target in First Half
articles.excerpt: The Centre's April-September deficit widened from Rs 5.7 lakh crore a year earlier as subsidy spending hit Rs 2.2 lakh crore on costlier petroleum and fertilisers, while capital expenditure rose to Rs 6.5 lakh crore, CGA data showed on Friday.
articles.nri_angle: The deficit path matters to NRI investors through rupee and bond-market pricing: at 42.1 percent of target at the half-year mark, the government has used less than half its full-year borrowing room.

articles.nri_angle: For NRI investors, the year's split verdict matters: large-cap India funds fell an average of 9.34 percent since last Diwali, while the small-cap gains were concentrated in a narrow set of stocks.
